title.narrative: Energy Access Advocacy Project in Africa

description.narrative: At the heart of transforming Africa’s energy landscape is the need for robust civil society engagement. Empowered civil society organizations (CSOs) can drive policy advocacy, foster community-led energy solutions, and hold institutions accountable, but their participation in MDB decision-making remains fragmented and under-resourced. The project targets several key challenges: 1. Underrepresentation of CSOs and communities: Most CSOs lack the technical knowledge, access, or resources to influence MDB processes or attend key forums. 2. Persistent fossil fuel financing: Ongoing MDB and public support for fossil projects delays clean energy transitions and exposes countries to fuel price volatility. 3. Underinvestment in DREs: Proven technologies remain underfunded, limiting access for last-mile communities. 4. Neglect of local innovators: Community-based enterprises face major financing and policy barriers, excluding marginalized groups from the transition. 5. Limited transparency and accountability: MDBs rarely publish timely, disaggregated project data, reducing public oversight. 6. Weak advocacy capacity: CSOs lack tools to track policy shifts, public sentiment, and influence outcomes. To close Africa’s energy gap, public finance must shift toward inclusive, community-driven DRE solutions. Empowering civil society and improving transparency are essential to ensuring that energy investments align with development, equity, and climate goals.
